tagline: Leading global offshore contract drilling services provider with one of the largest and most modern fleets
hero_kpi_rationale: The $4.7 B backlog is the key indicator of future revenue visibility for a drilling company, reflecting demand from major clients and the quality of the contract portfolio in a cyclical sector.

kpis.name: Total backlog
kpis.explanation: Total value of signed drilling contracts in progress, calculated by multiplying contractual day rates by contract duration
kpis.description: Backlog reflecting client commitments for drilling services. Increase of $1,063.8 M compared to February 2025, primarily due to contract extensions for floating drilling rigs.

kpis.name: Number of drilling rigs
kpis.explanation: Total number of drilling rigs operated by Valaris: 13 drillships, 2 semi-submersible rigs and 31 jackup rigs, plus 50% participation in 9 rigs through the ARO joint venture
kpis.description: Fleet of rigs directly owned by Valaris, one of the largest and most modern globally, including a world-class ultra-deepwater fleet and a premium jackup fleet.

kpis.name: Backlog - Floating rigs
kpis.explanation: Backlog for drillships and semi-submersible rigs
kpis.description: Backlog for floating rigs (13 drillships and 2 semi-submersibles). Increase of $1,006.8 M due to new contract extensions for various drillships.

kpis.name: Backlog - Jackups
kpis.description: Backlog for the jackup fleet (31 rigs). Decrease of $187.2 M due to revenue recognition and removal of backlog for one rig (VALARIS 120), partially offset by $590 M in new contracts.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Consolidated annual revenue, value extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $2.37 B in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $5.3 B in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of $1.16 B in the latest year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of $0.6 B in the latest year

kpis.name: Business Combination with Transocean
kpis.explanation: Business combination agreement signed on February 9, 2026, whereby Transocean acquires Valaris at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share
kpis.description: Major merger transaction via a Bermuda scheme of arrangement. Upon closing, current Transocean and Valaris shareholders will own approximately 53% and 47%, respectively, of the combined company. Closing is subject to regulatory approvals, shareholder vote and customary conditions. Outside date: February 9, 2027. Potential termination fees: $173 M in certain termination scenarios.

risks.title: Failure or delay of the merger with Transocean
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned first and repeated multiple times. The language is strong ("adversely affect", "material and adverse effect"). The merger is conditional on multiple approvals and a MAE. The Competition category is weighted because failure of the merger exposes the company to strategic vulnerability.

risks.title: Dependence on oil and gas prices
risks.score_rationale: Cited as a key performance factor, with repeated language on direct impact on demand, day rates and utilization. The risk is structural and recurring, intensified in 2026 by geopolitical tensions and climate policies. Weighted by macroeconomic significance.

risks.title: Intense competition for drilling contracts
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly stated as "highly competitive" and "cyclical", with direct impact on revenues. The language is firm but less alarming than for the merger. Market cyclicality reinforces severity. Category heavily weighted in the sector.

risks.title: Non-realization of backlog
risks.score_rationale: Backlog is presented as uncertain, with risk of termination, force majeure or non-payment. The amount is significant ($4.7 B) and the language emphasizes potential variances. Industrial category, less weighted than financial or strategic risks.

risks.title: Operational restrictions during the merger
risks.score_rationale: The risk is new and well-documented: the company cannot change strategy, invest or sign major new contracts. Language highlights impact on management and strategic decisions. Industrial category, but high strategic impact.

risks.title: Loss of key personnel or recruitment difficulties
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the context of uncertainty related to the merger. Language is moderate ("could adversely affect"). Less central than financial or operational risks, but recurring in 10-Ks. Category less weighted.

risks.title: Litigation related to the ongoing merger
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of litigation risks, negative publicity and management distraction. Language is preventive but serious ("could be distracting", "incur significant costs"). Litigation category moderately weighted.

ai_positioning.summary: Valaris does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
